checks: Each facet has a high vertex. The inset copy is a homothety of the tetrahedron of scale δ/4, has area fraction δ³/64, and every barycentric coordinate is at least δ/16. Its low sum is at most δ/2.
For mean one the four vertex values sum to four and M≤4+3η. If η≤δ/8 the inset gives an affine value at least δ/8, hence patch integral at least δ⁴/512.
If η>δ/8 the negative corner scale η/[2(M+η)] gives negative-part integral at least η⁴/[16(M+η)³]. Using M+η≤4(1+η), monotonicity, and (1+δ/8)³<2 gives the claimed 2⁻²³ constant.
The convex case uses φ≥ℓ₊, φ−ℓ≥ℓ₋ and mean ℓ=φ(g). Rearranging ε+patch≥a(I−ε) gives at least aI/(1+a)≥aI/2. The zero-mean support case has ε=I.

overlap.comparison: Its strip estimate is an upper bound for convex mass near a moving barycentric level. It does not give a lower observability bound on a designated shared patch or a quantitative affine negative-part dichotomy.

readability: The parts ℓ₋ and ℓ₊ are the standard nonnegative negative and positive parts. All facet integrals use normalized area.
review_method: Independent exact frozen proof and source-locator review, with symbolic arithmetic verification where applicable.
summary: Both stated constants follow from exact corner-area scaling and the affine support at the centroid, uniformly over all nonnegative continuous convex fields on the facet.
